chains.title: Weakened TGIF2/MEIS-class homeodomain site acting as a local repressor element near PELI2
chains.element: Unannotated intronic sequence at chr14:55887040, no overlapping cCRE

links.claim: Group G008 (Homeodomain) has 7 passing models of consistent sign; the best model is TGIF2's own model (z -38.69, effect -2.43, site 99.8th -> 94.1th percentile), so the alt T allele binds this specificity less. The qbic_tf_detail lookup of TGIF1 shows TGIF1's own model gives effect +0.176, z 3.51, which does NOT pass the gate and points the opposite way, so TGIF1 is not the member supported by the data; TGIF2 is named because it carries the strongest passing own model and is expressed in MCF7 (20.51 TPM), with MEIS3 (15.61 TPM, z -23.79) and PKNOX2 (not expressed) as alternatives within the same specificity.
No cCRE or regulatory feature overlaps the site (nearest dELS 1868 bp away) and GERP is -3.12, so a repressive element here is speculative and unsupported by cited data.

PELI2 is the nearest protein-coding TSS at 230.8 kb; this is proximity only. The single credible set at the variant is a brain eQTL for ENSG00000259868 (PIP 0.03), and no breast eQTL exists, so the gene link is unsupported.
TGIF2 and MEIS3 are expressed in MCF7, which gives expression context only; nothing cited shows the site is accessible or occupied in breast cells.

If TGIF2 acts as a repressor here, weaker alt binding would de-repress PELI2; however no GWAS association exists for this variant and the PELI2 literature is a thyroid-cancer prognostic gene list, not breast-cancer mechanism, so the phenotype link is unsupported.

chains.title: Loss of an XBP1 binding site in an unannotated element acting on PELI2
chains.element: Non-cCRE sequence ~1.9 kb from ENCODE dELS EH38E1716463
chains.cell_type: ER-positive luminal breast epithelium (MCF7 line as expression context)

links.claim: The only model in group G382 is XBP1's own model (z -91.69, effect -3.167): the alt T allele binds less in vitro, though the site falls only from the 100.0th to the 98.7th percentile, so a strong site remains. XBP1 is the sole TF in the group and is very highly expressed in MCF7 (636.57 TPM). Against this, ENCODE Factorbook shows no XBP1 peak containing or within 100 bp of the variant in MCF-7, which argues against in vivo occupancy (though absence may also mean no suitable experiment).
The variant is intronic with no overlapping cCRE and no regulatory feature, GERP -3.12; the nearest dELS is 1868 bp away with no cited linkage, so element function is unsupported.
PELI2 is the nearest protein-coding TSS (230.8 kb) but there is no PELI2 eQTL at this variant and no significant breast-tissue eQTL at all, so the gene assignment rests on proximity alone.

XBP1 is abundant in MCF7 (636.57 TPM), giving expression context only; no accessibility or occupancy evidence places the site in active chromatin in breast cells, and XBP1 is broadly expressed so luminal specificity is not demonstrated.
No GWAS association exists for this variant and the PELI2 literature cited concerns a thyroid-cancer prognostic signature, so no breast-cancer phenotype link is supported.

chains.title: Weakened CRE-like site (CREB1) with a distal effect on KTN1

links.claim: Group G062 (bZIP, CRE specificity) predicts weaker alt binding (CREB1 own model z -37.47, effect -2.019; CREM z -29.21). CREB1 is named because it has the highest expression among own-model members in MCF7 (30.28 TPM vs CREM 24.59; ATF1 is mapped only at 25.91 TPM); this is a choice on expression alone and does not exclude CREM or ATF1. Related CRE-binding groups G017 (CREB3 family) and G033 (ATF2/ATF7) show the same direction, so the prediction is a general loss of a CRE-like site rather than CREB1-specific.
No cCRE or regulatory feature overlaps the site and conservation is negative (GERP -3.12), so an active CRE here is not supported.
KTN1 is the second-nearest TSS at 328 kb and broadly expressed; no eQTL, contact or perturbation evidence links it to this site, and breast-tissue eQTL analysis is negative.
CREB1, CREM and ATF1 are expressed in MCF7, which is expression context only.
No GWAS association exists for this variant and no breast-cancer evidence connects KTN1 to this locus.

grades_v0.reason: Only a QBiC-SELEX prediction (E08): XBP1 own model, alt binds less, which is consistent with allele_binding_more=ref. A binding prediction alone is weak, and there is no ChIP or allelic assay. XBP1 expression (636.57 TPM) supports plausibility only.

E03 shows no cCRE overlap and E01 shows no regulatory feature, with GERP -3.12. The nearest dELS is 1868 bp away and has no linkage to this site. The chain itself calls element function unsupported, so the claim is not backed.

PELI2 is 230.8 kb away and merely the nearest listed TSS (E02). The only credible set (E05) is a brain eQTL for ENSG00000259868, not PELI2, with PIP 0.03. No looping, eQTL or CRISPR evidence links this site to PELI2.

E08 gives XBP1 expression of 636.57 TPM in MCF7, but nothing shows the site is accessible or active in MCF7. 'Luminal-specific' is over-claimed because XBP1 is broadly expressed, and the E07 and E08 expression values are not specific to luminal cells.

E04 reports 0 GWAS associations for this variant. E06 and E06a only list PELI2 as a prognostic gene in papillary thyroid carcinoma, which is not breast cancer. The direction of the PELI2 effect on risk is also unspecified.

E16 gives a QBiC-SELEX prediction only, with weaker alt binding for CREB1 own model (z -37.47), consistent with ref binding more. CREB1 was chosen from a group that also includes CREM and ATF1 (mapped) simply because it has the highest expression. No ChIP or allelic assay is cited.
E03 and E01 show no cCRE and no regulatory feature, and conservation is negative. The chain concedes the element is weak or cell-type restricted, so nothing supports an element at this site.

E02 only lists KTN1 at 328 kb, and the chain describes it as an alternative target. No eQTL, contact or perturbation evidence connects KTN1 to this variant, and the E05 credible set concerns a different gene.
E16 shows CREB1 expression in MCF7 (30.28 TPM), which is expression context only. There is no evidence of site activity in MCF7 or in breast epithelium.
E04 shows 0 GWAS associations, so it does not support a phenotype link. The chain itself admits no breast-cancer association is documented for KTN1 or this locus.

E09 gives a QBiC-SELEX prediction only. The best model in G017 is CREB3, and CREB3L4 is a lower-ranked member (z -37.55) with 48.8 TPM versus 45.81 for CREB3. The expression difference is negligible, and the claim that CREB3L4 is enriched in hormone-responsive epithelium has no cited evidence. The choice of TF is unjustified.
E03 and E01 show no cCRE overlap and no regulatory feature. The chain says the site is predicted in vitro only, so there is no element evidence.
E02 only gives PELI2 as the nearest TSS at 230.8 kb. E05 shows no PELI2 eQTL, only a brain eQTL for another gene, so there is no link to PELI2.
E09 gives expression of CREB3L4 and CREB3 in MCF7, which is context only. Nothing shows the site is active in MCF7, and 'luminal' specificity is not shown.
E06 and E06a are generic and the PELI2 hit is from thyroid cancer prognostics. E04 shows no GWAS association. The chain itself says the literature is not mechanistic.

E13 gives a QBiC-SELEX prediction only. The best model is TGIF2, not TGIF1, and TGIF1 is chosen as a covered family member on expression grounds alone (39.86 TPM). The TGIF1 TF in E13 is covered by its own model, but no TGIF1 passing model is named among the members shown, so the TGIF1 binding change is not shown. Treating TGIF2 results as TGIF1 evidence is unjustified.
E03 and E01 show no cCRE and no feature. A silencer function is speculative and nothing cited supports it.
E02 gives only distance (230.8 kb) for PELI2. Direction rests on an assumed repressor role for TGIF1 that is not cited, and no eQTL or perturbation data link the site to PELI2.
E13 gives TGIF1 expression in MCF7 (39.86 TPM), which is context only and does not show repression or site activity there.
E06 and E06a do not bear on breast cancer risk through PELI2 upregulation. E04 shows no GWAS association, and the chain concedes no direct evidence.

next_experiment: Query existing ENCODE MCF-7 data at chr14:55887040 for (a) DNase/ATAC accessibility and (b) TGIF2/MEIS-family ChIP-seq peaks. This costs nothing beyond a database lookup and directly separates the top two chains: the null predicts closed, unbound chromatin, whereas H4 requires an accessible, homeodomain-occupied element. If a peak and accessibility are found, follow with the allelic luciferase reporter plus TGIF2 knockdown in MCF7.
